segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: There are many theories contrary to what Mike has argued,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: but there isn't time tonight to look at them all.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: I will instead present the one theory I think is most probably correct,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: which I only have time to summarize.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Shortly after the death of Jesus,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: his disciples prayed,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: meditated and searched the Scriptures for some meaning to justify the tragedy,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: and some way to preserve and promote the noble program of moral reform Jesus had died for.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: As a result some had prophetic dreams or visions in which Jesus appeared to them,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: reassuring them and telling them just what they wanted to hear-that he had been raised by God so all who attached themselves to him and his moral program would participate in his resurrection as soon as this good news was preached to all Israel.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: The relevant content of this belief was that Jesus had been granted a new body by God.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: The resurrection body promised to all the faithful,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: abandoning his old body to the grave like a shell or husk,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: to return to the dust from which it came.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: But the new body lived in heaven,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: from where Jesus would soon return on clouds of glory to give us our own new bodies at the end of days.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Such,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: I believe,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: was the original belief; but the Church quickly fragmented into competing sects with different agendas,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: and over the first century some groups became more and more gnostic while others became more and more sarcicistic.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Gnosticism gravitated to the view that only the soul of Jesus was exalted.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Well,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Sarcissism was the opposite view; that Jesus was raised only in the flesh,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: in the very same body that died and was buried.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: I believe both views are distortions of what the original Christians believed; yet both arose at roughly the same time and place.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Just as the Gnostics developed novel legends to explain and justify their view of things,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: so did the Sarcicists.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: The canonical Gospels represent the parables and legends adopted or developed to serve the Sarcicist programme,

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: and that was the one and only sect to obtain total power and preserve for posterity its documents and its own version of history.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: That is my theory in rough outline.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Now I have to explain why my theory is a better explanation of the facts than Mike's.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: There are nine facts that together establish that my theory is more probably correct.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Number one.

segments.speaker: Richard Carrier
segments.text: Paul contradicts the gospels of Luke and John by describing a spiritual resurrection.
